title: Continuous subspaces and quotients of finite-dimensional p-adic representations
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite intermediate field $E\subseteq\Omega$ with its $\ell$-adic topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $\Pi$ be a profinite group (a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group). Use continuous finite-dimensional $E$-representations and equivariant $E$-linear maps as in [def-pod-l-adic-representations](2); all vector spaces have their usual finite-dimensional $\ell$-adic topology.

For a continuous representation $V$ and a $\Pi$-stable $E$-linear subspace $U\subseteq V$, the subspace is closed, its subspace topology and the quotient topology on $V/U$ agree with their usual finite-dimensional $E$-vector-space topologies, and the induced actions on $U$ and $V/U$ are jointly continuous. The inclusion $U\to V$ and quotient $V\to V/U$ are equivariant continuous linear maps.

For every equivariant $E$-linear map $h:V\to W$ of continuous representations, put $K=\ker h$, $I=h(V)$ and $Q=W/I$. With the induced actions, $K,I,Q$ are continuous finite-dimensional $E$-representations and the canonical sequences
$$0\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow V\longrightarrow I\longrightarrow0,\qquad 0\longrightarrow I\longrightarrow W\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow0$$
are equivariant and exact on underlying vector spaces. The canonical maps $K\to V$ and $W\to Q$ satisfy the kernel and cokernel universal properties among these continuous representations.

source.place: Corollary 6.8.5, proof, p. 60: the category of representations of the profinite fundamental group on finite-dimensional E-vector spaces admits kernels and cokernels. This node states the topological linear-algebra input of that sentence, independently of any sheaf realization.

proof.text: Equip E with its spectral nontrivially normed field structure using the topology equality in the statement. The finite-dimensional module topology on V is Hausdorff: the coordinate linear map for Module.finBasis is continuous by IsModuleTopology.continuous_of_linearMap and injective. Finite-dimensional subspaces are closed by Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional, and their subtype topology is the module topology by isModuleTopologyOfFiniteDimensional. Construct the restricted action with Representation.subrepresentation, converted from linear endomorphisms to automorphisms using Representation.asGroupHom and generalLinearEquiv. Its joint continuity is the ambient action composed with the product of identity and subtype, then restricted to the subtype.

source.place: Corollary 6.8.5, proof, p. 60; finite-dimensional subspace input expanded using the cited Mathlib topology lemma

proof.text: Construct the quotient action with Representation.quotient and the same automorphism conversion. Mathlib supplies the quotient topological module operations and IsModuleTopology.instQuot. The product of identity on G and the quotient projection is an open quotient map by Submodule.isOpenQuotientMap_mkQ and IsOpenQuotientMap.prodMap. Its continuous_comp_iff reduces joint continuity of the quotient action to continuity of the projection composed with the ambient action. Transport joint continuity to the module topology in IsContinuousCoefficient using eq_moduleTopology. Inclusion and projection are equivariant by their construction and continuous by continuous_subtype_val and Submodule.continuous_mkQ.

source.place: Corollary 6.8.5, proof, p. 60; quotient action descended along the open quotient map

proof.text: Equivariance of h shows ker h and range h are invariant: h(ρ(g)a)=σ(g)h(a). Apply the preceding proved private subquotient construction to ker h in V and range h in W. This gives the induced continuous actions, module topologies, and equivariance/continuity of the inclusions and projection. The original h is continuous by LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional and its range corestriction is continuous by Continuous.subtype_mk. Equivariance of the corestriction follows from equivariance of h and the injective range inclusion.

source.place: Corollary 6.8.5, proof, p. 60; kernels, images and cokernels of equivariant maps

proof.text: The subtype maps are injective by Subtype.val_injective; rangeRestrict is surjective by LinearMap.surjective_rangeRestrict; mkQ is surjective by Submodule.mkQ_surjective. The first sequence is exact by LinearMap.exact_iff, LinearMap.ker_rangeRestrict and Submodule.range_subtype; the second is LinearMap.exact_subtype_mkQ. This proves both exact sequences with the continuous equivariant maps constructed above.

source.place: Corollary 6.8.5, proof, p. 60; underlying exact sequences

proof.text: For h.comp f=0, use LinearMap.codRestrict to construct f' into ker h; its composite with the inclusion is definitionally f. Equivariance follows by applying Subtype.ext to equivariance of f and of the inclusion, and continuity follows from continuity of f into V and Continuous.subtype_mk. Any second factor agrees pointwise after inclusion, hence agrees by subtype injectivity and LinearMap.ext. For g.comp h=0, show range h ≤ ker g and construct g' with Submodule.liftQ. Its factorization equation is Submodule.liftQ_mkQ. For equivariance and uniqueness choose preimages under the surjective quotient projection. Continuity follows from IsModuleTopology.continuous_of_linearMap using the quotient module topology and the target topological module structure.
